notes: The circuit image shows direct wires between the boards, with a 4.7k pull-up resistor from each of A5 (SCL) and A4 (SDA) to 3V3. The image does not show how the mini breadboards are used, so I put both pull-ups and the SCL/SDA junctions on bb1: A5 wires share column 5 and A4 wires share column 10. The resistors' other legs go to the top power rail, which is fed from the reader's 3V3 pin.
The second mini breadboard (bb2) is listed in the parts but is not used in the circuit image, so it has no connections.
Only 6 of the 10 listed jumper wires are needed for the circuit shown.
The catalogue has no USB port on the Nano or ports on usb-cable, so the USB edges have no port names. Each board is powered and connected to the computer by its own USB cable.
The image labels the GND pin on each board without saying which of the two GND pins it is, so I used GND_1 on both. The '3V' label is taken as 3V3. A4 is SDA and A5 is SCL, as the manual states.
The pull-up resistor value is 4.7k, so I set value=4700. The catalogue resistor entry is named 100 ohm, but the value prop overrides that.
